sources.title: Introducing Fugu Max and Fugu Ultra v2
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. September 11 release identifies Fugu Ultra v2, says it shares the core orchestration architecture with Max and uses a swappable pool of open and specialized workers. It reports no nominal total, active count or sized orchestrator backbone. The introductory multi-trillion-parameter example is generic, not a Fugu specification; one-line parameter change refers to API selection.

sources.title: Sakana API models and endpoints
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. The exact fugu-ultra-v2.0 entry and fugu-ultra alias binding remain explicit. Ultra uses a fixed worker pool and bills orchestration tokens, but the documentation supplies neither a neural parameter count nor a named sized v2 backbone. API request parameters and token usage are not learned-weight counts.

sources.title: Pinned official integration model catalog
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. The pinned fugu-ultra entry is named Fugu Ultra v2.0 and specifies 1000000 context, text/image input, high/xhigh reasoning and parallel tool calls. This integration contract contains no learned-weight count, neural dimensions or named base checkpoint.

sources.title: Sakana AI API Platform Terms of Service
sources.evidence: Service/configuration intellectual property remains with Sakana and relevant licensors. Permission is limited to use of the service; no right to redistribute model weights is granted.

sources.title: Sakana Fugu Technical Report, June revision
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. Section 3.2 says original Fugu-Ultra builds on the Conductor framework, adding long-horizon function calling and adaptive agent memory. It describes GRPO and natural-language worker orchestration without naming a sized base model. Full-text parameter/base-model searches and comparison tables supply no Ultra v2 total or active count; this June paper predates September Ultra v2.

sources.title: Sakana Fugu report revision history
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. arXiv history lists June 19 submission and June 23 revision. The suffix v2 denotes the June paper revision, not the September Fugu Ultra v2 model.

sources.title: Gemma 4-based Fugu orchestration experiment
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. The August 10 original identifies earlier Fugu orchestrators only as Qwen-based, without a version or size. It explicitly tests a separate Gemma 4 E2B orchestrator to demonstrate backbone modularity. Neither statement identifies the September Ultra v2 backbone, so no E2B or Qwen size is inherited.

sources.title: Recursive self-improvement through multi-agent self-supervision
sources.evidence: Later October research trains a shared Qwen3.6-27B model in a separate recursive self-improvement experiment. It does not identify that model as Ultra v2 or supply an exact Ultra v2 comparison count.

sources.title: Sakana Chat update: Fugu Max and memory
sources.evidence: Reopened successfully October 27. The September 17 English/Japanese announcement puts Fugu Max in Sakana Chat and adds memory. It names no sized Ultra v2 backbone or parameter count.

sources.title: Official repository inventory
sources.evidence: Complete, nontruncated tree contains integration configuration, scripts, demos and a technical report, with no distributed neural checkpoint. Official SakanaAI Hugging Face fugu search also returned an empty list.

sources.title: Sakana AI research and product archive
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27 and followed later first-party product/research leads through the current October 27 archive. MASS, Chat, the GTM interview, Open House and Product Team material do not publish a total or active count for the exact Ultra v2 model.

sources.title: Learning to Orchestrate Agents in Natural Language with the Conductor
sources.evidence: Freshly opened October 27. Section 4.1 explicitly describes a 7B Conductor trained from Qwen2.5; Appendix A.1 names Qwen2.5-7B. Its model-scale analysis also studies a 3B variant. These are experimental Conductor checkpoints. The Fugu report inherits the framework, not an explicitly identified checkpoint, and neither paper binds 7B or 3B to September Ultra v2.

sources.title: Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision
sources.publisher: Sakana AI and research collaborators / arXiv
sources.evidence: Freshly opened October 27. Section 4.1 specifies Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 with qwen-code 0.20.0 for the MASS experiment. Reviewed model/setup and comparison material; Ultra v2 is not identified as this checkpoint or given a nominal total/active row. A later research experiment does not establish deployed Fugu lineage.

sources.title: Taking Japan-Born AI Products to the World: An Interview with Sakana AI’s VP of GTM
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 original interview describes Fugu coordinating multiple frontier models. It supplies no Ultra v2 checkpoint identity, nominal total or active count.

sources.title: Sakana AI Engineer Open House 2026
sources.evidence: Freshly opened October 27. October 21 event report describes Fugu as research-developed orchestration deployed by the Product Team; no Ultra v2 base model or parameter size is given.

sources.title: Inside Sakana AI’s Product Team
sources.evidence: Freshly opened October 27. September 17 team/process interview contains no Fugu Ultra v2 model identity or total/active parameter disclosure.

name.note: Official release name; direct API identifier is fugu-ultra-v2.0.

developer.note: Sakana develops the orchestrator; its worker models may have different developers.

family.note: Normalized Fugu product family, distinct from a claim about underlying backbone lineage.

release_date.note: Dated announcement explicitly states immediate API availability. June original Ultra and July v1.1 are earlier revisions.

open_weights.note: Hosted proprietary release. Public integration code and open worker models do not distribute the complete Ultra v2 orchestrator/system weights.

license.note: Classification of the hosted service; no worker, client repository or paper license is transferred to the model.

parameters_b.note: Fresh original releases/docs, named-lineage checks, later research tables and bounded exact-name searches found no nominal total for Ultra v2 or a sized base explicitly tied to it. Sharing an orchestration framework does not identify a checkpoint. Conductor Qwen2.5-7B/3B, Gemma4 E2B and MASS Qwen3.6-27B are separate experiments, not v2 lineage; worker-pool sizes are not summed.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh active-count searches and original research comparisons found no explicit nominal activated-parameter value or counting convention for exact Ultra v2. No inference is made from dense totals, earlier experimental backbones, worker counts or billed orchestration tokens.

architecture.note: Learned multi-model orchestration is documented, but exact v2 backbone neural topology is undisclosed. A worker pool is not a neural mixture-of-experts checkpoint. June report GRPO and August Qwen lineage cannot be asserted as exact September v2 architecture.

context_window.note: Official v2.0 integration entry advertises 1,000,000 tokens. This is composed-service context capacity, not proof that the orchestrator or every worker natively supports that length.

modalities.note: Verified text/image input and text response interface. PDF is a file container rather than a separate neural modality; no native PDF encoder is established. Service image support does not establish a vision encoder inside the orchestrator.

reasoning.note: Exact v2.0 entry supports high/xhigh; API documents max as an alias of xhigh and exposes reasoning controls. This describes the composed service.

tool_call.note: Model-selected function tools/tool_choice and built-in web search are documented, with parallel calls enabled. Internal orchestration and external caller-executed function calls are distinct.

description.value: Orchestration model that coordinates a fixed pool of worker models for complex reasoning, research and software tasks.
description.note: Replaces promotional quality framing with documented purpose and fixed worker-pool behavior, without assigning unsupported benchmark superiority or architecture.

patch.notes: Released September 11, 2026 as Fugu Ultra v2; fugu-ultra currently aliases fugu-ultra-v2.0. The 1,000,000-token context, text/image input, reasoning and tool calls describe the composed API service. Total and active parameters remain undisclosed, with no sized backbone explicitly tied to v2. The June paper revision v2 concerns original Ultra; Conductor Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma4 E2B and MASS Qwen3.6-27B are separate experiments. Independent worker models are not a neural MoE parameter count. Exact backbone topology remains undisclosed.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retained null total and active counts after freshly reopening the exact September release, API docs/config, June report/history, Gemma experiment, Conductor and later MASS papers, Chat update and current archive/interview leads. Bounded searches for exact Ultra v2 total, active and sized-base disclosures found none. Framework inheritance does not bind the separate 7B, 3B, E2B or 27B experiments to v2. Added explicit null parameter patches and parameters_source; the other twelve field assessments are unchanged.
